checks.finding: Every requirement (REQ-001 through REQ-011) is backed by acceptance criteria verified against concrete, inspectable artifacts (file text, tool registry, test-suite pass/fail) rather than vague intent. The new REQ-005 warn-on-divergence resolution (specs/mcp-readonly-preflight/requirements.md:144) is backed by AC-027a (requirements.md:148-151, testable via the agent's output text) and AC-027b (requirements.md:153-156, testable via the behavioral conclusion acted on), each with a corresponding TEST row (acceptance-tests.md:38-39). REQ-007's dual-runtime ACs (AC-017-020, requirements.md:187-197) state observable path-execution outcomes even though the exact verification method is deferred to OQ-009 (requirements.md:199); per calibration this is acceptable because the specification states the observable criterion and the harness/method belongs to a later gate.

Every stated goal traces to at least one AC. The Overview's two obligations (probe creation, policy gap-fill) map to REQ-001/002 and REQ-008/009 respectively. The newly-added warn-on-divergence goal ('the agent states the disagreement visibly to the operator, and proceeds on the file-based conclusion', requirements.md:144) maps directly to AC-027a (states disagreement + names source acted on, requirements.md:148-151) and AC-027b (conclusion acted on is the file-based one, requirements.md:153-156).

AC-027a and AC-027b (requirements.md:148-156) describe concretely observable artifacts: output text containing a disagreement statement and a named source (AC-027a), and a specific behavioral outcome of which conclusion was acted on (AC-027b), mirroring the observable pattern already established at AC-012/AC-013. TEST-027a/TEST-027b (acceptance-tests.md:38-39) split these into two independently-failing assertions, consistent with the document's established practice of avoiding weak-half passes (e.g., TEST-001/002, acceptance-tests.md:58-66). Minor stylistic note only, not blocking: unlike AC-012/AC-013, which were explicitly split per skill 'because a single criterion could be satisfied by testing whichever skill is easier (sweep 4)' (requirements.md:140), AC-027a/AC-027b are not split per skill and their TEST rows target 'both skills' in a single row without the explicit AND-required disclaimer used for the analogous AC-004-007 pattern ('asserted independently against both skills... not a partial pass', requirements.md:104). This does not clear the Finding Evidence Gate as a FAIL because the document's repeatedly-stated sweep-4 convention (invoked ~6 times) makes the stricter, both-skills-required reading clear from context even without a restated disclaimer at AC-027a/b specifically.

requirements.md:244-252 states seven explicit Non-goals (no write/approval tools, no rewriting existing prose, probe never authoritative, no MCP server implementation changes, no server registration, no ADR generalization, no interviewer-skill addition). The new REQ-005 resolution does not expand scope: AC-027b (requirements.md:153-156) explicitly forecloses a 'warn, then follow the probe' reading, keeping intact the existing Non-goal that 'the probe never selects the feature, never advances a gate' (requirements.md:248).

Baseline Constraints BL-001 through BL-005 (requirements.md:272-276) state implementation-boundary, behavioral-preservation, prose-preservation, protected-file/approval, and registry constraints. The new resolution states its own constraint explicitly: 'the file-based flow stays authoritative either way... warning cannot change an outcome it is forbidden from changing' (requirements.md:146), and AC-027b operationalizes that the run proceeds normally on the file-based conclusion in the divergent case, precluding the divergence warning from being read as a blocking or error condition (distinct from REQ-004's fallback-error guarantee).

High-risk claims each have a stated validation surface: no-write preservation -> AC-014-016 (requirements.md:170-177); outcome invariance -> AC-012/AC-013 (requirements.md:134-138); protected-file conformance -> AC-025/AC-026 (requirements.md:233-237); and the newly-resolved authority-inversion risk in the divergence branch -> AC-027b (requirements.md:153-156) / TEST-027b (acceptance-tests.md:39), which is explicitly designed to fail an implementation that 'warns, then follows the probe'.
